recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. The current source satisfies FHIR-12223 after later terminology clarifications; further required-binding refinements should proceed under later issues such as FHIR-51935, not this DSTU2 wording fix.
issue_request: FHIR-12223 was a Published, Persuasive FHIR-core vocab issue requesting that the required binding definition be changed from wording that said instances of the element SHALL include a code from the value set, because that could be read as requiring the element to appear even when cardinality permits absence.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 10435, represented in git as 0579550ad80c4ef88eb1432d46033e0e68d0c346, which adjusted the required-binding wording in the then-current terminology/conformance pages. No prior Issue-Reconcile-Key commit for FHIR-12223 was found on the combined branch before this audit.
additional_context: Later Published FHIR-12444 clarified the short required-binding description and added the datatype-specific criteria note; that issue is already audited on the combined branch. Later Published FHIR-27144 clarified the expansion wording and has already been reconciled on the combined branch. FHIR-51935 is a later Resolved - change required R6 clarification for Coding/repetition details and is background only for this applied/published run.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/terminologies.html no longer has the old 'instances of this element SHALL include a code' wording; it uses concept wording in the Binding Strengths table, explicitly points to datatype-specific criteria, and its Required Binding Strength section says the data element contains a value in the bound value set expansion. The CodeableConcept bullets require at least one Coding and state text alone is not a substitute.
